name: distal radius and scaphoid fractures overview
title: A fall on an outstretched hand: a distal radius fracture is judged on X-ray as crooked, short or not smooth and treated by closed reduction and casting, or surgery when reduction is inadequate; a scaphoid fracture is suspected even with a normal X-ray, cast when undisplaced or distal and operated when displaced or proximal

root.title: Fall on an outstretched hand (FOOSH): which bone, and does it need SURGERY?
lines: treatment is dictated by age and activity level, and by how displaced the fracture is

groups.title: DISTAL RADIUS: very common
lines: localized pain · poor function if the anatomy is not restored

groups.title: SCAPHOID: young people
lines: retrograde blood flow → nonunion, osteonecrosis, late arthrosis

pres.title: X-ray: 3 questions
lines: • CROOKED? normal 12° palmar tilt on the lateral
• SHORT? more than neutral ulnar variance (compare the other side)
• SMOOTH? a step > 1 mm → post-traumatic arthrosis

pres.title: Be SUSPICIOUS
lines: • X-ray NORMAL → treat as fractured + CT or MRI

head: h
CLOSED reduction + cast
forgiving at the extremes of age
inv: traction → INCREASE the deformity (unlocks the fragments) → correct it
tx: well moulded does NOT mean tight

head: h
SURGICAL reduction
still crooked, short or not smooth
inv: • crooked: radio-ulnar joint motion altered, rotation restricted
tx: Open reduction internal fixation (ORIF) or external fixation

head: h
Cast
undisplaced, or distal pole
inv: A normal X-ray can hide it
lecture case: CT showed the line
tx: lecture case: healed on CT at 8 weeks

head: h
Surgery
displaced, or proximal pole
tx: volar approach · screw on the post-op X-ray
